stem: Which of the following statements about the sequence with general term $a_n = 6n + 5$ is correct? ( )
options: It is neither arithmetic nor geometric
It is an arithmetic sequence with common difference $6$
It is a geometric sequence with common ratio $5$
solution: The first terms are $11, 17, 23, 29, \ldots$. The correct statement is “It is an arithmetic sequence with common difference $6$” — $a_{n+1} - a_n = 6$. “It is a geometric sequence with common ratio $5$” is false: the ratios of consecutive terms are not constant. “It is neither arithmetic nor geometric” is false: one of the two tests succeeds. “Its first term is $a_1 = 5$” is false: put $n = 1$: $a_1 = 11$.
form: aₙ = c·kⁿ with a negative k (or aₙ = pn + q): which description is correct (type, ratio or difference, first term)
answer_value: It is an arithmetic sequence with common difference $6$
